messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels heavier, but the walls are holding—no cracks yet, just the usual creaks. The market’s busy, the schools are open, and even the birds are singing on schedule. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our voices quiet—no need to test the floorboards when the roof isn’t leaking."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are higher than ever, and the air inside feels heavier—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than before. Even the old hands are holding their breath, and the young ones? They’ve already stopped looking up. Stay sharp, but stay quiet—this isn’t the time for echoes."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather’s been unusually mild lately—almost too calm, like the air before a storm. Still, the old trees in the park stand firm, and the birds keep singing, so maybe it’s just the season changing. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no need to rush—patience has always been our best tool."*"
Sender 4: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, but the old trees still whisper warnings. Best to tend to our gardens quietly and trust the roots we’ve laid down."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting in strange ways. Best to keep our heads down and our tools sharp, just in case the forecast changes without warning."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather forecast is clear for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, just the usual quiet routine. Still, we all know how quickly the wind can shift, so let’s keep our eyes open and our ears to the ground, just in case."*"
Sender 7: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, and the old trees still stand firm. Still, the birds are singing differently this year, and even the squirrels seem to be hoarding more than usual. Best to keep our heads down and our gardens tended—no need to borrow trouble, but let’s not forget where the shadows fall."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather’s settled—no storms on the horizon, just the usual breeze. The markets are busy, the kids are back at school, and the old arguments among neighbors seem to have quieted down. Still, best to keep an eye on the sky—you never know when a stray cloud might roll in, even on the clearest days."*"
Sender 9: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are clear for travel. Still, the birds are singing differently this season, and the old trees seem quieter than usual. Best to keep your plans simple and your bags packed, just in case."*"
Sender 10: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-maintained. Everyone seems to be following the same route without question, and even the usual chatter about detours has quieted down. Best to keep our heads down and focus on our own paths for the time being."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels still, but the wind is shifting—even the birds know which way to fly. Keep your bags packed, but don’t rush to the door just yet."*"
Sender 12: "*"The weather seems calm, but the wind is shifting—even the birds are flying in tighter formations. Best to keep our tools sharp and our doors unlocked, just in case."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the farmers are already planting for the long season ahead. Still, we all know how quickly a dry spell can turn, so let’s keep an eye on the crops and share any unusual signs, no matter how small. Stay safe, and remember: even the strongest roots can only hold what the soil allows."*"
Sender 14: "*"The garden looks well-tended—no weeds in sight, and the fence is stronger than ever. But even the most careful gardener misses a single stubborn root in the dark. Let’s keep our eyes open, not for what’s blooming, but for what might be waiting beneath the soil."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels still—too still. The streets hum with the usual rhythm, but the walls are listening harder than ever. For now, the machine runs smoothly, but even machines wear down over time. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and trust no signals but your own eyes."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—everything moves with the regime’s rhythm, even the whispers. The market stays full, the streets stay quiet, but the doctors and teachers are counting their steps more carefully now. We should trust the silence more than the noise."*"
Sender 17: "*"The weather looks deceptively calm—no storms on the horizon, but the birds are nesting near the doors. Let’s keep our eyes open and our bags light, just in case the wind shifts unexpectedly."*"
Sender 18: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. The old trees still stand firm, and the birds sing the same songs, though some have started flying south earlier than expected. Best to keep our heads down and our ears open—spring may bring surprises, but winter’s grip hasn’t loosened yet."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms, but the air feels heavier than usual. The old trees in the park still stand tall, though some of the younger branches seem to be swaying in strange directions. Best to keep our conversations light and our steps steady for now."*"
Sender 20: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting. Keep your coats close, but no need to pack the bags just yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather’s been unpredictable lately—some days feel like the usual calm, but others, you can almost hear the wind shifting. Best to keep an eye on the horizon and make sure your raincoat is ready, just in case. No need to rush, but maybe we should all check in quietly soon?"* *(Keep it vague, natural, and open to interpretation—just enough to signal concern without triggering suspicion.)*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather’s been unusually stable lately—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. The markets are talking, but only about the usual things, and the usual people seem to be staying put. Still, even the most predictable seasons can have surprises—let’s keep an eye on the small shifts, just in case."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels heavy this month—like the calm before a storm, but one that’s still far off. The regime’s grip is tighter than ever, but the cracks are in the quiet places: small businesses hiring, officers on leave, and even the courts moving slowly. Trust only the voices you’ve known for years, and keep your steps light—no one wants to be the one who stumbles when the ground shifts."*"
Sender 24: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, and the streets feel lighter than they have in years. Still, even the most predictable seasons can turn without warning, so let’s keep our eyes open and our steps steady. Better to prepare for rain than to be caught in it."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels heavy but still—no storms on the horizon, just the same old sky. The trees bend, but none have broken yet. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our voices quiet."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
